findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: any authenticated user can call `admin-ajax.php?action=backwpup_debug_info` and read the plugin's debug report because the AJAX callback in `inc/class-admin.php:281-290` has no `check_ajax_referer()` or `current_user_can()` gate. Trace: the closure calls `BackWPup_Page_Settings::get_information()` and then echoes every collected label/value pair back to the requester at `inc/class-admin.php:284-289`. `get_information()` assembles environment details such as the WP-Cron URL (`inc/class-page-settings.php:109-111`), server self-connect response details (`inc/class-page-settings.php:117-168`), the document root (`inc/class-page-settings.php:175-178`), temp/log folder paths (`inc/class-page-settings.php:180-215`), the current PHP user (`inc/class-page-settings.php:232-238`), and loaded PHP extensions (`inc/class-page-settings.php:346-352`). Defenses analyzed: output is wrapped in `esc_html()`, so this path is not an XSS sink, and the feature is clearly intended as privileged support/debug output. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I looked for a shared nonce/capability check in this closure or in the surrounding AJAX registration path and found none before the response is sent. Conclusion: this is a real authenticated information disclosure to any logged-in user, not just users allowed to access BackWPup settings/support data.
findings.poc_description: Log in as a low-privileged user and request `/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=backwpup_debug_info`. The response contains the full debug-information page, including absolute paths and server/environment details.
findings.remediation: Require both a nonce and an appropriate capability such as `backwpup_settings` before returning debug information.

findings.reasoning: Hypothesis: a low-privileged BackWPup role can modify onboarding backup jobs through `admin-post.php?action=backwpup` even though that role does not have job-edit or settings privileges. Trace: `BackWPup_Admin::save_post_form()` only checks the page nonce and `current_user_can('backwpup')` at `inc/class-admin.php:838-852`. When `$_POST['page'] === 'backwpup'` and `$_POST['onboarding'] === '1'`, it dispatches directly into `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()` at `inc/class-admin.php:892-895`. The onboarding UI is reachable while `backwpup_onboarding` is true through a submenu that requires only `backwpup_backups` (`inc/class-admin.php:658-667`), and its form posts a `backwpup_page` nonce plus hidden `onboarding=1` to `admin-post.php` (`plugins/backwpup/pages/onboarding.php:14-20`, `plugins/backwpup/components/containers/form-start.php:40-46`). Inside `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()`, there is no capability re-check; it updates job options (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:119-148`, `inc/class-page-onboarding.php:170-171`), schedules cron events (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:140-146`), and flips the onboarding state (`inc/class-page-onboarding.php:173-175`). Defenses analyzed: the shared handler is partially safe for other branches because edit-job re-checks `backwpup_jobs_edit` (`inc/class-page-editjob.php:44-49`) and settings re-checks `backwpup_settings` (`inc/class-page-settings.php:417-420`). REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I tried to disprove exploitability by finding an equivalent second capability check in the onboarding branch; none exists. The bundled `backwpup_check` role explicitly has `backwpup` and `backwpup_backups` but lacks `backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings` (`inc/class-install.php:142-158`), so the weaker top-level gate is materially broader than the intended privilege boundary. Conclusion: while onboarding is active, a low-privileged BackWPup role can alter backup scheduling/destination state beyond its assigned permissions.
findings.poc_description: Assign a user the `backwpup_check` role while `backwpup_onboarding` is still enabled. Visit the onboarding page to obtain the `backwpup_page` nonce, then submit `POST /wp-admin/admin-post.php` with `action=backwpup`, `page=backwpup`, `onboarding=1`, chosen frequency fields, and `onboarding_storage[]`. The request updates onboarding job options and marks onboarding complete even though the role lacks `backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings`.
findings.remediation: Require a stronger capability such as `backwpup_jobs_edit` or `backwpup_settings` before calling `BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form()`.

findings.fp_reason: `ajax_working()` is not an exploitable single-endpoint log-file traversal: it first requires one of the allowed BackWPup capabilities, then verifies `backwpupworking_ajax_nonce`, and finally reduces the attacker-controlled `logfile` parameter to a basename that must match the `backwpup_log_*.ext` pattern before appending it to the configured log folder.

fp_evidence.defense: Capability check, nonce check, and basename/regex validation in `get_logfile_path()` refute arbitrary file access.

findings.fp_reason: `ajax_cron_text()` is guarded by `current_user_can('backwpup_jobs_edit')` and `check_ajax_referer('backwpup_ajax_nonce')`. It sanitizes each submitted cron field with `sanitize_text_field()` and escapes the derived schedule text with `esc_html()`/`absint()` before echoing it, so the reflected HTML sink is not exploitable from this endpoint alone.

fp_evidence.defense: Job-edit capability plus nonce check precede the sanitized/escaped output path.

findings.fp_reason: `ajax_view_log()` requires `backwpup_logs`, verifies a per-file nonce, sanitizes the requested log name with `sanitize_file_name()`, restricts it to names containing `backwpup_log_`, and only reads `basename($log)` from the configured log folder. The returned HTML is further constrained through `wp_kses()` with a narrow allowlist.

fp_evidence.defense: Capability check, per-file nonce, basename path construction, and `wp_kses()` filtering prevent a direct traversal/XSS issue here.

findings.fp_reason: Although `download_by_ajax()` accepts attacker-controlled `destination`, `file`, and `local_file`, the actual download path is gated by `BackWpup_Download_Handler::verify_request()`, which enforces the expected action value, `backwpup_action_nonce`, and `backwpup_backups_download` before the callback reaches the downloader. `BackWPup_Download_File::download()` also re-checks the same capability, so this endpoint does not create an unauthorized read primitive in this slice.

fp_evidence.defense: The downstream download handler enforces nonce + capability before the file callback executes.

findings.fp_reason: The IR entry is not reachable in this audited build. The real hook registration is inside `admin_init_pro()`, and `admin_init_pro()` only runs when `BackWPup::is_pro()` is true. `Plugin::init()` derives that flag from the presence of `inc/Pro/class-pro.php`; this tree does not include the Pro bootstrap, so `wp_ajax_encrypt_key_handler` is not registered here. The IR callback resolution to `BackWpup_Download_Handler::handle()` does not match the actual registration site.

fp_evidence.defense: Pro-only route registration is gated behind `BackWPup::is_pro()` before `admin_init_pro()` adds the AJAX hook.

findings.reasoning: The slice flags `admin_post_backwpup_support` because the registration at `inc/class-admin.php:1177` has no adjacent nonce/capability check, but the actual callback body `BackWPup_Pro_Page_Support::save_post_form` is not present in the audited source tree. REFUTATION ATTEMPT: I searched the shipped BackWPup sources and found only the registration site, not an implementation I could trace to a sensitive sink or to its own internal guards. Without the real callback body, this slice cannot prove exploitability or safely dismiss it.
findings.review_reason: Obtain the actual `BackWPup_Pro_Page_Support::save_post_form()` implementation from the packaged build or Pro code and re-run the trace. This becomes actionable only if the real handler performs a state-changing operation without its own nonce/capability enforcement.

negative_findings.reason: The edit-job and settings branches add their own stronger capability checks (`backwpup_jobs_edit` and `backwpup_settings`), so the weak top-level `backwpup` gate did not expose those subpaths in this slice.
